meta.name: Monitor exposed secrets in GitHub and CI logs with WhatsApp alerts

parameters.content:
## Secrets & API Key Exposure Monitor

Scans recent Git activity and CI/CD logs for accidentally committed credentials, checks whether flagged secrets are STILL LIVE against their issuing provider, and runs a genuine remediation loop: alert -> human confirms they've rotated it -> a timed grace period -> automatic re-verification -> either close the case or escalate again if the key is somehow still active.

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add credentials: your Git host API (repo node), your CI/CD platform API (CI logs node), a generic auth for the verification node (it's reused for GitHub/Stripe-style bearer-token checks), and WhatsApp Business Cloud API credentials on every WhatsApp node
3. Edit Set - Config: repoOwner/repoName/baseBranch, ciApiUrl, whatsappBusinessPhoneId, whatsappRecipientPhone
4. Point Wait - For Remediation Confirmation's resume webhook at your on-call tool's 'mark rotated' action
5. Activate the workflow, or use the Manual Trigger to test end to end

### Requirements
- Git hosting API access (commits/diffs)
- CI/CD platform API access (build logs)
- WhatsApp Business Cloud API credentials

### A note on the raw secret value
The actual matched string is kept ONLY in an internal field used to test validity against the issuing provider — every outward-facing message (WhatsApp text, the report payload) uses the masked value exclusively. Turn off execution-data logging or use n8n's data-pruning settings for this workflow, since even internal fields are still part of execution history.

### How to customize
- Add more regex patterns (Azure, Twilio, SendGrid, npm tokens, etc.) to the first code node
- Wire the 'cloud' verification branch to a properly SigV4-signed AWS call (STS GetCallerIdentity) instead of the illustrative placeholder
- Adjust the severity score weights or the grace-period duration in Wait - For Re-Verification Grace Period

## 1. Trigger, Data Sources & Detection

Set - Config centralizes every API URL and the WhatsApp sender details.

HTTP Request - Fetch Recent Repository Commits/Diffs and HTTP Request - Fetch CI/CD Pipeline Logs are the first two of the workflow's three API calls, pulling raw text to scan.

JS - Scan Content for Secret Patterns & Compute Entropy Scores is the first code node: ~10 named-provider regexes plus a Shannon-entropy filter on generic key=value assignments, deduped and masked, emitted as one item per finding so everything downstream (verification, severity routing) runs per-secret.

## 2. Switch-Routed Verification

Switch - Secret Type Category is the first switch: cloud/VCS/payment findings each get routed through a small Set node that configures a different target URL and auth header, then all three converge on the SAME HTTP Request - Verify Credential Validity call (the workflow's third API node) — one shared verification node, dynamically configured per finding. Generic high-entropy matches can't be verified against a specific provider, so they skip straight to risk classification instead.

This same verification node is reused later for the post-remediation re-check — IF - Is Reverification Pass tells the two passes apart and routes each to the right next step.

nodes.name: Sticky Note - Severity Routing & Remediation Loop

parameters.content:
## 3. Risk Scoring, Severity Switch & Remediation Loop

JS - Classify Risk & Build Remediation Plan is the second code node: scores severity from secret type, source (repo vs. CI), live/revoked status, and builds a per-type remediation checklist.

Switch - Severity Routing is the second switch: critical/high goes into the full loop, medium gets a single WhatsApp notice, low gets logged only.

The loop: WhatsApp - Send Urgent Alert -> Wait - For Remediation Confirmation (webhook resume) -> IF - Remediation Confirmed (unconfirmed loops back to the same Wait after a reminder) -> Wait - For Re-Verification Grace Period (a genuine TIME-based wait, not webhook resume) -> Set - Prepare Reverification -> back through the shared verification call -> IF - Still Valid After Remediation decides between escalating again or closing the case as confirmed-revoked.
